title: Homily II — Zion, where she lay

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily II on the Dormition, col. 729 (PDF leaf 406)

source_text: Οὐκ ἄτοπον δέ μοι δοκεῖ λόγῳ διαγράψαι ὅσον ἔχει πρὸς δύναμιν, καὶ εἰκάσαι, καὶ τύπῳ σχηματίσαι τὰ ἐπὶ τῇ ἱερᾷ ταύτῃ τοῦ Θεοῦ μητρὶ τετελεσμένα θεάματα, ἃ μετρίως, καὶ λίαν συνοπτικῶς, τὸ δὴ λεγόμενον, παῖς ἐκ πατρὸς ἄνωθεν παρειλήφαμεν. Δοκῶ γάρ μοι ταύτην τὴν ἁγίων ἁγιωτέραν, καὶ ἱερῶν ἱερωτέραν, καὶ ὁσίων ὁσιωτέραν, τὴν γλυκεῖαν τοῦ μάννα στάμνον, πηγὴν δὲ μᾶλλον εἰπεῖν ἀληθέστερον ἀνακεκλίσθαι ἐπί τινος σκίμποδος ἐν τῇ θείᾳ καὶ περιωνύμῳ πόλει Δαβὶδ, Σιὼν φημὶ τῇ περιόπτῳ καὶ περικλεεστάτῃ, ἐν ᾗ πεπλήρωται μὲν ὁ νόμος τοῦ γράμματος, ὑπηγόρευται δὲ ὄνομα τοῦ πνεύματος· ἐν ᾗ τὸ Πάσχα τὸ τυπικὸν ὁ νομοδότης Χριστὸς ἐκτετέλεκε, καὶ Πάσχα τὸ ἀληθὲς ὁ παλαιᾶς καὶ νέας διαθήκης Θεὸς παραδέδωκεν· ἐν ᾗ τὸ δεῖπνον μυστικὸν τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ μαθηταῖς ὁ ἀμνὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ αἴρων τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου μεμυσταγώγησε, καὶ τούτοις ἑαυτὸν οἷα μόσχον σιτευτὸν τέθυκε, καὶ τῆς ἀληθινῆς ἀμπέλου τὸν βότρυν ἐληνοβάτησεν· ἐν ᾗ Χριστὸς τοῖς ἀποστόλοις ὀπτάνεται ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνιστάμενος, καὶ Θωμᾶν πιστοῦται, καὶ διὰ τούτου τὰ πέρατα, ὡς εἴη Θεός τε καὶ Κύριος, δύο φύσεις φέρων ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ μετὰ τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναβίωσιν, καὶ ταύταις καταλλήλους δύο ἐνεργείας, αὐτεξούσιά τε θέσματα, εἰς αἰῶνα τὸν ἄπειρον αἰωνίζοντα. Αὕτη τῶν Ἐκκλησιῶν ἡ ἀκρόπολις· αὕτη τῶν μαθητῶν καταγώγιον· ἐν ταύτῃ τοῦ παναγίου Πνεύματος ἡ πολύηχος, καὶ πολύγλωσσος, καὶ πυρίμορφος ἐπιφοίτησις τοῖς ἀποστόλοις ἐκκέχυται· ἐν ταύτῃ ὁ Θεολόγος τὴν Θεοτόκον παρειληφὼς, ἐλειτούργει τὰ δέοντα· αὕτη ἡ μήτηρ τῶν ἀνὰ πᾶσαν τὴν οἰκουμένην Ἐκκλησιῶν, τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ Μητρὸς ἐνδιαίτημα πέφηνε, μετά γε τὴν τοῦ υἱοῦ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναφοίτησιν· ἐν ταύτῃ τοίνυν ἡ μακαρία Παρθένος ἐπί τινος τρισολβίου κλίνης κατέκειτο.
pass_a_gloss: It does not seem to me out of place (ἄτοπος) to sketch (διαγράφω) in word as far as is in [my] power, and to liken/picture (εἰκάζω), and to shape in outline the sights (θεάματα) accomplished (τελέω) for this holy Mother of God, which moderately and very concisely, as the saying goes, child from father, we have received from of old (ἄνωθεν). For I think (δοκῶ μοι) that she, holier than holy ones, more sacred than sacred ones, more saintly than saintly ones (ὅσιοι), the sweet jar (στάμνος) of manna, or rather to say more truly the spring (πηγή), reclined (ἀνακλίνω) on a pallet (σκίμπους) in the divine and famous city of David, I mean Zion, conspicuous (περίοπτος) and most glorious, in which the law (νόμος) of the letter (γράμμα) was fulfilled (πληρόω), and the name of the spirit was dictated/declared (ὑπαγορεύω); in which Christ the lawgiver (νομοδότης) completed (ἐκτελέω) the typical (τυπικός) Passover (Πάσχα), and the God of old and new covenant (διαθήκη) handed down the true Passover; in which the Lamb (ἀμνός) of God who takes away the sin of the world initiated his disciples into the mystical (μυστικός) supper (δεῖπνον), and sacrificed (θύω) himself to them as a fatted calf, and trod in the winepress (ληνοβατέω) the cluster (βότρυς) of the true vine (ἄμπελος); in which Christ, rising from the dead, is seen (ὀπτάνομαι) by the apostles, and assures (πιστόω) Thomas, and through him the ends (πέρατα), that he is God and Lord, bearing two natures (φύσεις) in himself even after the return to life (ἀναβίωσις) from the dead, and two operations (ἐνέργειαι) corresponding to them, and self-determining wills, lasting (αἰωνίζω) into the endless age. This [is] the citadel (ἀκρόπολις) of the Churches; this the lodging of the disciples; in her the many-sounding (πολύηχος), many-tongued and fire-formed (πυρίμορφος) visitation of the all-holy Spirit was poured out (ἐκχέω) on the apostles; in her the Theologian (Θεολόγος), having taken the Mother of God (Θεοτόκος), ministered (λειτουργέω) what was needed; she, the mother of the Churches throughout the whole inhabited world (οἰκουμένη), appeared (φαίνομαι) as dwelling (ἐνδιαίτημα) of the Mother of God, after the Son's going-up again from the dead; in her then the blessed Virgin lay (κατάκειμαι) on a thrice-blessed (τρίσολβιος) bed (κλίνη).
pass_b_english: It does not seem out of place to me to sketch in words, as far as I am able, to picture and to outline the wonders that were accomplished for this holy Mother of God, which we have received from of old, son from father, as the saying goes, in modest measure and very briefly. For I picture her, holier than the holy, more sacred than the sacred, more saintly than the saints, the sweet jar of manna (Hebrews 9:4), or rather, to speak more truly, its spring, lying on a pallet in the divine and famous city of David, I mean Zion, renowned and most glorious; where the law of the letter was fulfilled and the name of the spirit was proclaimed; where Christ the Lawgiver completed the Passover that was a figure, and the God of the old and new covenant handed down the true Passover; where the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29), initiated his disciples into the mystical supper, sacrificed himself for them like a fatted calf (Luke 15:23), and trod in the winepress the cluster of the true vine (John 15:1); where Christ, risen from the dead, appears to the apostles and assures Thomas (John 20:27–28), and through him the ends of the earth, that he is God and Lord, bearing two natures in himself even after his return to life from the dead, and two operations that answer to them, with wills that are free, enduring into the endless age. This city is the citadel of the Churches; this is the lodging of the disciples; in her the coming of the all-holy Spirit, with many sounds, in many tongues and in the form of fire, was poured out on the apostles (Acts 2:1–4); in her the Theologian took the Mother of God to himself (John 19:27) and ministered to her needs; this mother of the Churches throughout the world became the dwelling of the Mother of God after her Son rose again from the dead. Here, then, the blessed Virgin lay on a thrice-blessed bed.

choices.note: Doubtful reading: the print has 'ὑπηγόρευται δὲ ὄνομα τοῦ πνεύματος' ('the name of the spirit was proclaimed').

The contrast with 'the law of the letter' would expect νόμος ('the law of the spirit', compare Romans 8:2 and 2 Corinthians 3:6); re-checked at 600 dpi, the print clearly reads ὄνομα, while the facing Latin has 'lex spiritus dictata est'; the English follows the print and the possible echoes are left uncited.

Printed 'αὐτεξούσιά τε θέσματα' is rendered 'with wills that are free': θέσμα means 'ordinance', but John's two-natures, two-operations, two-wills formula expects θελήματα; re-checked at 600 dpi: the print clearly reads θέσματα, and the facing Latin of the same column has 'liberasque voluntates', so the English keeps 'wills'.
'The Theologian' is John the Evangelist; the name is not in the Greek and is not supplied in the reading text.

John 15:1 (the true vine) and John 19:27 (the disciple took her to his own home) are cited from their wording though not in the print's margin; the margin's John 20:28 is cited with verse 27 because the passage speaks of Thomas being assured.
Hebrews 9:4 (the jar of manna) is cited as the clear figure behind 'the sweet jar of manna' (compare Exodus 16:33).
The Last Supper Passover (Luke 22:15) is narrated, not quoted; left uncited.
